neighbours.label: a first- or second-person possessive or pronoun (our, my, your, we) opening a point in advisory or institutional prose, against the same points phrased in the third person
fire:
When choosing a school, consider these points:
1. Your child's interests and strengths.
Gossip is taken very seriously in this community. Our elders teach that words can wound.

Before you start the medication, ask questions.
Your doctor can explain the side effects.

Before hiring a contractor, I weighed several things:
1. My budget for the whole project.
We take privacy seriously. Our policy explains how we store and share your details.

If the pain returns, do not wait.
Your nurse is available by phone at any hour.
Our faith asks for patience in hard times. We are taught to forgive those who hurt us.

To plan a trip on a budget, think about:
1. My own limits on time and money.
